term: ground of a necessary existential disjunction
resolution: "Ground of the disjunction" is used in four senses that the map keeps apart. A local ground (DEF-LOCAL-GROUND) is some reason at each world and may vary; a uniform ground (DEF-UNIFORM-GROUND) is one reason at every accessible world; the instance reading (DEF-INSTANCE-GROUNDING) restricts what a reason may be to an individual's existence fact; an efficient producer is the separate Ontic.Causes relation (DEF-PSR-EXTERNAL-CAUSE, see DISAMB-PSR-EXPLANATION-CAUSE). The results never pass from one to another: local to uniform fails in the truthmakers model; uniform to a necessary being needs the instance reading as a listed premise and fails without it in the lawGround model; neither model nor the positive fixedBearer model has any causation, so no reason is read as a cause. Explains keeps the bare, nonnecessitating sense of DEF-PSR-STRENGTH-REASON; Necessitating is a separately listed property that the truthmakers and lawGround models satisfy, so necessitation of the disjunction by its grounds does not supply a necessarily existing ground. Which sense a source intends is not decided here.
